source.title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems

accepted.question_text: For each positive integer n, let R_n^∞ be the maximum Banach–Mazur distance d_BM(X, ℓ_∞^n) over all n-dimensional Banach spaces X. Determine the asymptotic behavior of R_n^∞ as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. (Distance from the cube – A. Pe lczy´nski [65]) Determine the asymp￾totic behavior of Rn∞ as n tends to infinity.

accepted.question_text: For 0 < δ ≤ 1, let K(δ) be the infimum of the real numbers K such that every normalized weakly null sequence has a δ-near unconditional subsequence with constant K. Does there exist a constant M > 1 such that K(δ) ≤ M for every 0 < δ ≤ 1?

evidence.quote: For each 0 < δ 6 1 let K(δ) be the infimum of the set of real numbers K such that every normalized weakly null sequence has a δ-near unconditional subsequence with constant K.
Problem 2. (Elton unconditionality constant – S. J. Dilworth, E. Odell, Th. Schlumprecht and A. Zs´ak [21]) Does there exist M > 1 such that K(δ) 6 M for every 0 < δ 6 1?

accepted.question_text: A normalized basic sequence (x_n) in a Banach space is called a Rosenthal basis if every normalized block sequence (v_n) of (x_n) has a subsequence equivalent to (x_n). Must every Rosenthal basis be equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 ≤ p < ∞?

evidence.quote: There is a slightly weaker notion: a normalized basic sequence (xn) in a Banach space X is said to be a Rosenthal basis if every normalized block sequence (vn) of (xn) has a subsequence which is equivalent to (xn).
Problem 3. (Rosenthal basis problem – H. P. Rosenthal [26]) Is it true that every Rosenthal basis (xn) is equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c0 or ℓp for some 1 6 p < +∞?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a reflexive Banach space such that all normalized weakly null sequences in X generate, up to equivalence, a unique spreading model; equivalently, |SP_w(X)/∼| = 1, where SP_w(X) denotes the class of spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences in X. Must that unique spreading model be equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 ≤ p < ∞?

evidence.quote: For every Banach space X let SPw(X) be the class of all spreading models generated by a normalized weakly null sequence in X and denote by ∼ the usual equivalence relation of equivalence of basic sequences.

Problem 4. (Unique spreading model problem – S. A. Argyros [2]) Let X be a reflexive Banach space such that |SPw(X)/ ∼ | = 1 (i.e. all normalized weakly null sequences in X generate a unique spreading model up to equivalence). Is it true that the unique spreading model is equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c0 or ℓp for some 1 6 p < +∞?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a reflexive Banach space with at most countably many equivalence classes of spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences; that is, |SP_w(X)/∼| ≤ ℵ_0. Does X contain a normalized weakly null sequence generating a spreading model equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 ≤ p < ∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. (Countable spreading models problem – S. J. Dilworth, E. Odell and B. Sari [20]) Let X be a reflexive Banach space such that |SPw(X)/ ∼ | 6 ℵ0. Does there exist a normalized weakly null sequence in X generating a spreading model equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c0 or ℓp for some 1 6 p < +∞?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a Banach space X has a normalized block homogeneous Schauder basis, meaning that every normalized block sequence of the basis spans a subspace isomorphic to X. Must X be isomorphic to c_0 or to ℓ_p for some 1 ≤ p < ∞?

evidence.quote: A normalized Schauder basis (xn) of a Banach space X is said to be block homogeneous if every normalized block sequence (vn) of (xn) spans a subspace isomorphic to X.
Problem 6. (Block homogeneous basis problem – see [27]) Let X be a Banach space with a normalized block homogeneous Schauder basis. Is it true that X is isomorphic to c0 or ℓp for some 1 6 p < +∞?

accepted.question_text: If X is a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space, does there exist a sequence (X_n) of subspaces of X that are pairwise non-isomorphic?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. (G. Godefroy [33]) Let X be a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space. Is it true that there exists a sequence (Xn) of subspaces of X which are pairwise non-isomorphic?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separable Banach space that fails type 2−ε, or fails co-type 2+ε, for some ε > 0. Must X contain continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces?

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Let X be a separable Banach space which fails to have type 2 − ε (or fails to have co-type 2 + ε) for some ε > 0. Is it true that X contains continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces?

accepted.question_text: Is every complemented subspace of C[0,1] isomorphic to a space C(K) for some closed subset K of [0,1]?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. (Complemented Subspace Problem for C[0, 1] – see [12, 52, 63]) Is it true that every complemented subspace of C[0, 1] is isomorphic to a C(K) space for some closed subset K of [0, 1].

accepted.question_text: Let T: C[0,1] → C[0,1] be a bounded linear operator, and let X be a separable Banach space that does not contain a copy of c_0. If T fixes a copy of X, must T fix a copy of C[0,1]? Equivalently, must the dual operator T* have non-separable range?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. (Fixing properties of operators on C[0, 1] – H. P. Rosenthal [69]) Let T : C[0, 1] → C[0, 1] be a bounded linear operator and X be a separable Banach

space not containing a copy c0. Assume that the operator T fixes a copy of X. Is it true that T fixes a copy of C[0, 1]? Equivalently, is it true that the dual operator T∗ of T has non-separable range?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space that is boundedly distortable, meaning distortable for some λ > 1 but not arbitrarily distortable for all λ > 1?

evidence.quote: A distortable Banach space X is said to be arbitrarily distortable if it is λ-distortable for every λ > 1; otherwise, X is said to be boundedly distortable.
Problem 11. (Bounded distortion – see [62]) Does there exist a boundedly dis￾tortable Banach space?

accepted.question_text: Is Tsirelson’s space T, or its dual, boundedly distortable rather than arbitrarily distortable?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. (Distortion of Tsirelson’s space – H. P. Rosenthal) Is T (or its dual) boundedly distortable?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separable Banach space such that every separable Banach space is Lipschitz isomorphic to a subset of X. Must X contain a copy of c_0?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. (Converse Aharoni problem – see [11, 44]) Let X be a separable Banach space with the property that every separable Banach space is Lipschitz iso￾morphic to a subset of X. Is it true that X contains a copy of c0?

accepted.question_text: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space X have an infinite-dimensional quotient that has a Schauder basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. (S. Banach [10] – A. Pe lczy´nski [64]) Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space X has an infinite-dimensional quotient with a Schauder basis?

accepted.question_text: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a non-trivial infinite-dimensional separable quotient?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. (Separable quotient problem) Does every infinite-dimensional Ba￾nach space have a non-trivial infinite-dimensional separable quotient?

accepted.question_text: For a given infinite-dimensional Banach space X, what is the greatest possible length of a Schauder basis that a quotient of X can have?

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Given an infinite-dimensional Banach space X, what is the longest Schauder basis a quotient of X can have?

accepted.question_text: Assume the P-ideal dichotomy, namely that for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of some set S, either there is an uncountable set T ⊆ S such that every countable subset of T belongs to I, or S can be decomposed into countably many pieces with no infinite subset in I. Under this assumption, are the following equivalent: (1) every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system; and (2) b = ℵ_2, where b is the minimum cardinality of an unbounded family in N^N under eventual domination?

evidence.quote: P-ideal dichotomy (PID): For every P-ideal3 I consisting of countable subsets of some index-set S, either (1) there is an uncountable set T ⊆ S such that every countable subset of T belongs to I, or (2) the set S can be decomposed into countably many subsets that have no infinite subsets belonging to I.
2Recall that b is the minimal cardinality of a subset of NN which is unbounded in the ordering of eventual dominance.
Problem 17. Are the following equivalent assuming the P-ideal dichotomy? (1) Every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system. (2) b = ℵ2.

accepted.question_text: A support set in a Banach space X is a nonempty convex set C such that every point x in C is a support point, meaning there is a functional f on X with f(x) = inf{f(y) : y ∈ C} < sup{f(y) : y ∈ C}. Which Banach spaces admit support sets? In particular, does every non-separable Banach space admit a support set?

evidence.quote: Recall that a support set in a Banach space X is a nonempty convex set C with the property that every point x of C is its support point, i.e. there is a functional f of X such that f(x) = inf{f(y) : y ∈ C} < sup{f(y) : y ∈ C}.
Problem 18. (S. Rolewicz [67]) Which Banach spaces admit support sets? Do all non-separable Banach spaces have support sets?

accepted.question_text: Does every Banach space of density strictly greater than ℵ_1 have a support set?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. (S. Todorcevic [79]) Does every Banach space of density > ℵ1 have a support set?

accepted.question_text: Does every Banach space X of density greater than the continuum c contain an infinite unconditional basic sequence? Does the answer change if one imposes additional assumptions such as reflexivity?

evidence.quote: Problem 20. (Unconditional basic sequences in non-separable spaces) Does every Banach space X of density > c have an infinite unconditional basic sequence? Does additional properties, like reflexivity, make a difference?

accepted.question_text: Does every Banach space of density greater than c, and does every reflexive Banach space of density greater than ℵ_1, contain an infinite sub-symmetric basic sequence?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Does every (respectively, every reflexive) Banach space of density > c (respectively, of density > ℵ1) has an infinite sub-symmetric basic sequence?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a non-separable Tsirelson-like Banach space, that is, a non-separable analogue of the classical Tsirelson construction based on a suitable non-separable analogue of the Schreier family?

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Is there a non-separable Tsirelson-like space?
This problem seems related to the existence of a nonseparable analogue of the Schreier family on which the Tsirelson construction could be based.

accepted.question_text: Is there a compact hereditary family F of finite subsets of ω_1 that contains every singleton and has the property that every finite subset of ω_1 contains a member of F of at least half its size?

evidence.quote: Problem 23. (D. H. Fremlin [29]) Is there a compact hereditary family of finite subsets of ω1 containing the singletons and having the property that every finite subset of ω1 has a subset half of its size belonging to the family F?
